_comment: Dollars per agent and model profile. The event's own cost is primary; the editable price list is a cross-check and a fallback for gateway events that carry no cost.
name: cost-per-agent
title: Cost per agent and model
description: What each agent spent, in dollars. The figure reported by the request itself is used whenever it is present; otherwise the price list mirrored from pricing.json is applied to the token counts and the result is labelled derived. A profile that appears in neither shows an empty cost, never a zero - a zero would read as 'this model is free' when the truth is 'nobody knows what this cost'.
af_decision_o4: O-4 (view delivery) is hybrid: files on disk plus a best-effort dashboard push. See README.md.
af_assumptions: COLUMN SPELLINGS AND JOIN VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE BACKEND, THIS QUERY NOT EXECUTED: during review of PR #567 OpenObserve v0.91.3 was stood up from the pinned artifact and the per-step token view's query was run verbatim, confirming the ingest naming this view also relies on. This view's own query was NOT among those executed. This view computes max(af_step_seq) inside its step_windows CTE but never orders on it or emits it, so it is deliberately left uncast. A dashboard already published under this title is never replaced by a re-run of quickstart.sh, so an existing factory keeps the query it first received — re-import this file by hand to pick up changes. CI has no backend, so none of this is re-verified automatically.

The native claude_code.api_request shape (input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd) is the synthetic fixture's hypothesis, not a recorded capture - see internal/telemetry/testdata/synthetic/api_request_events.json, which P6b replaces. Whether these arrive as OTel logs or metrics is also an inference; if it is metrics, the stream name and column prefix both change.

Attribute names are rewritten on ingest. Trace resource attributes are prefixed with 'service_' and every dot becomes an underscore, so af.formula_instance is queryable only as service_af_formula_instance. OTLP logs do NOT get the prefix, so the same attribute is af_formula_instance on the native-event side of the join. _timestamp is microseconds while start_time/end_time are nanoseconds and duration is microseconds.

The model dimension on both sides is the models.json PROFILE name, not a model id: resolveRecordModel returns cfg.Agents[agent] or cfg.Default, and af.model carries the same value. pricing.json is therefore keyed by profile name, and a profile with no priced row renders NULL.
cost_usd_micros is named in the design but does not appear in the recorded fixture, so no query depends on it.

dashboard.title: Cost per agent and model
dashboard.description: Dollars per agent, reported first and derived only as a fallback.

queries.query:
WITH published_prices AS (
    -- Mirrors pricing.json in this directory, which is the copy the operator edits; a test keeps
    -- the two identical. Keys are models.json PROFILE names, because that is what the telemetry
    -- carries - there is no model id anywhere in the signal. A profile absent from this list is
    -- absent on purpose: the LEFT JOIN below then misses and the dollar renders NULL. That is the
    -- whole point - an unknown model must read as "we do not know", never as "this model is free",
    -- which is what a zero default would say.
    SELECT * FROM (VALUES
        ('default', 15.00, 75.00),
        ('opus-4-8', 15.00, 75.00),
        ('sonnet-5', 3.00, 15.00),
        ('gpt-4o', 2.50, 10.00)
    ) AS t(model_profile, input_per_mtok_usd, output_per_mtok_usd)
),
spend AS (
    SELECT af_formula_instance AS formula_run,
           af_agent            AS agent,
           af_model_profile    AS model_profile,
           count(*)            AS requests,
           sum(input_tokens)   AS input_tokens,
           sum(output_tokens)  AS output_tokens,
           -- The event's own cost is the primary source. It is summed separately from the
           -- derivation so the two can be compared rather than silently blended.
           sum(cost_usd)       AS cost_usd_reported,
           count(cost_usd)     AS requests_carrying_cost
    FROM "logs"."default"
    WHERE af_overhead IS NULL OR af_overhead = ''
    GROUP BY af_formula_instance, af_agent, af_model_profile
)
SELECT s.formula_run,
       s.agent,
       s.model_profile,
       s.requests,
       s.input_tokens,
       s.output_tokens,
       s.cost_usd_reported,
       CASE
           WHEN p.model_profile IS NULL THEN NULL
           ELSE (s.input_tokens  / 1000000.0) * p.input_per_mtok_usd
              + (s.output_tokens / 1000000.0) * p.output_per_mtok_usd
       END AS cost_usd_derived,
       -- Event first, table second. There is no zero-defaulting anywhere in this expression: when
       -- neither source knows the price the answer is NULL and the basis column says why.
       CASE
           WHEN s.requests_carrying_cost > 0 THEN s.cost_usd_reported
           WHEN p.model_profile IS NULL THEN NULL
           ELSE (s.input_tokens  / 1000000.0) * p.input_per_mtok_usd
              + (s.output_tokens / 1000000.0) * p.output_per_mtok_usd
       END AS cost_usd,
       CASE
           WHEN s.requests_carrying_cost = s.requests THEN 'reported'
           WHEN s.requests_carrying_cost > 0          THEN 'reported (partial)'
           WHEN p.model_profile IS NULL               THEN 'unpriced profile - dollars NULL, not zero'
           ELSE 'derived'
       END AS cost_basis
FROM spend s
LEFT JOIN published_prices p ON p.model_profile = s.model_profile
ORDER BY s.formula_run, s.agent
